summary: The North Lands crowns: the tier C tree of 22 small crowns between Sonargur and Parim, with the Compact, the shore and the Houses.

own_counsel.name: Our Own Counsel
own_counsel.desc: The crown of [ROOT.GetName] takes its advice at home and answers to nobody for the habit.

two_shore_trade.name: Trade with Both Shores
two_shore_trade.desc: Merchants of [ROOT.GetName] sell to Sonargur and to Parim and are welcome in both.

grain_and_fish_spirit.name: Grain and Fish
grain_and_fish_spirit.desc: Barley and salt herring keep the larders of [ROOT.GetName] full through the longest winter.

market_fairs_spirit.name: Market Fairs
market_fairs_spirit.desc: Traders from three coasts come to the midsummer fair of [ROOT.GetName], and the whole realm profits from the noise.

fisherfolk.name: Boats and Nets
fisherfolk.desc: Tarred hulls and strong nets feed the coast of [ROOT.GetName] and put new hands to work.

shore_watch.name: The Shore Watch
shore_watch.desc: Every beacon from cape to river mouth answers the next, and nothing comes ashore unannounced.

forest_trails_spirit.name: Forest Trails
forest_trails_spirit.desc: Lanterns at the trailheads and hunters for guides: the forests of [ROOT.GetName] are friends to its own and foes to strangers.

island_crown_spirit.name: An Island Crown
island_crown_spirit.desc: The sea is the only road to [ROOT.GetName], and its people know every yard of it.

freeholders_moot.name: The Freeholders' Moot
freeholders_moot.desc: Every free farmer has a voice at the open-air moot, and what he hears there he keeps.

freeholders_moot_2.name: Old Rights Kept
freeholders_moot_2.desc: The old rights are read aloud each Glernaen, and every freeholder of [ROOT.GetName] knows exactly what he is owed.

free_towns.name: The Free Towns' Council
free_towns.desc: The burghers of [ROOT.GetName] tax themselves, build their own walls and listen to one another.

lords_men.name: The Lord's Men
lords_men.desc: Stewards and sworn knights run the realm to the lord's measure, and the council is glad of the quiet.

leren_banner.name: Under the Leren Banner
leren_banner.desc: A Leren garrison and a Leren drillmaster have made the crown's host steadier, if not any freer.

compact_member.name: The Compact Member
compact_member.desc: A seat in the Leren Compact opens the harbours of Sonargur and the purses of its friends.

dark_strait_watch.name: Across the Dark Straits
dark_strait_watch.desc: Watchers on the south-western headlands note every sail from the Dark Lands.

dark_shore_trade.name: Traders of the Dark Shore
dark_shore_trade.desc: Furs, salt fish and iron go south, and silver of doubtful pedigree comes north.

houses_watched.name: A Watchful Crown
houses_watched.desc: The crown reads the ledgers of the Houses and the faces of their almoners, and has decided to trust neither.

north_at_war.name: The North at War
north_at_war.desc: The beacons are lit and the muster rolls are open. The crown of [ROOT.GetName] is ready, and knows it is not alone.

a_crown_asks_to_join.title: [FROM.GetName] Asks for a Seat
a_crown_asks_to_join.desc: Envoys of [FROM.GetName] have come to Sonargur with gifts and a letter asking for a seat in the Leren Compact. They have waited three days in the antechamber, and say they are willing to wait longer.

a_northern_crown_asks_for_a_shield.title: [FROM.GetName] Asks for Parim's Shield
a_northern_crown_asks_for_a_shield.desc: [FROM.GetName] fears the stronger crowns of the North and asks the court at Parim to stretch a shield over it. Its envoy stands in the hall and does not say what the crown will give in return.

black_sails_seen.title: Black Sails Seen
black_sails_seen.desc: Fishermen tell of black sails among the far islands. They were seen at dusk, low on the water and moving against the wind, and by morning they were gone.

the_almoners_in_the_north.title: The Almoners in the North
the_almoners_in_the_north.desc: Grey-robed almoners have opened their doors in the market town, with a ladle of broth for every beggar and a bandage for every wound. The townsfolk are wary of strangers, but they cannot fault their manners.

whispers_from_the_holds.title: Whispers from the Holds
whispers_from_the_holds.desc: Traders returning from the Dark Lands say that gifts are arriving in the orc holds from the south: silver, good iron and strange embassies. They cannot say who sends them, only that he has patience.

a_northern_crown_keeps_faith.title: [FROM.GetName] Keeps Faith
a_northern_crown_keeps_faith.desc: While the greater crowns of the North turn away, [FROM.GetName] writes to Parim that it holds to the old alliance, and that its companies will come south if Parim wishes them.

focuses.name: The Crown of [ROOT.GetName]
focuses.desc: [ROOT.GetName] is a small crown between two great ones. Sonargur holds the northern shore of the strait and Parim the southern, and a lordship that means to outlast them both must learn which to heed, and when.

focuses.name: Look to Sonargur
focuses.desc: The ships of Lerendor pass this shore all summer, and their captains dip a pennant to anyone who dips one back. [ROOT.GetName] lowers its banner to Sonargur first, and trusts the Leren court to remember who bowed early.

focuses.name: Look to Parim
focuses.desc: Parim is the greater market, and its silver is older and cleaner than the Leren kind. [ROOT.GetName] writes to the court by the Great Lake, and does not mention that it reads Sonargur's letters too.

focuses.name: Our Own Counsel
focuses.desc: The crown has no wish to be anyone's lesser. [ROOT.GetName] takes its counsel at home before it takes it abroad, and tells both great courts, politely, that the answer will come when it is ready.

focuses.name: Ask for a Seat in the Compact
focuses.desc: The Leren Compact is a hall of two seats and a great many requests. [ROOT.GetName] sends a letter to Sonargur asking for a place in it, and offers its harbours and its good opinion in exchange.

focuses.name: Envoys to Parim
focuses.desc: An envoy of [ROOT.GetName] rides south with a letter and a modest gift to ask for the shield of Aenor. Whether a shield is offered, and what it costs, is a matter for the court at Parim.

focuses.name: Join the Free Crowns
focuses.desc: The Free Crowns of the North are a promise rather than an alliance: every crown keeps its own hall and its own banner. [ROOT.GetName] adds its name to the roll and agrees to answer when another crown calls.

focuses.name: Trade with Both Shores
focuses.desc: Sonargur buys fish and furs and Parim buys timber and wool. [ROOT.GetName] sells to both, quarrels with neither, and finds that a merchant is welcome in any harbour that profits by him.

focuses.name: A Crown Among Crowns
focuses.desc: After years of careful courtesy, [ROOT.GetName] is known in every northern court and owed something by most of them. Its envoys are seated, its seals honoured and its voice, for a small crown, carries far.

focuses.name: Hearth and Harbour
focuses.desc: The hearth is the heart of every northern hall, and the road to market is its lifeline. [ROOT.GetName] raises a new Guild Workshop in its capital and straightens the road that leads from it.

focuses.name: Timber Rights
focuses.desc: The forests belong to the crown, and the crown grants the right to cut them in careful measure. A timber yard now turns each winter's felling into beams and planks for half the North.

focuses.name: Village Roads
focuses.desc: Mud swallows carts in the thaw, and the northern roads have always been poor. [ROOT.GetName] sets gangs to lay gravel and split logs in the worst places, and carts come through in a day instead of a week.

focuses.name: Northern Smithies
focuses.desc: Iron comes down from the hills and goes out again as blades, helms and nails. The smiths of [ROOT.GetName] are given a hall of their own in the capital, with a new Armoury at its heart and a rule that no apprentice leaves before he can forge a true edge.

focuses.name: Grain and Fish
focuses.desc: Barley in the valleys and herring in the cold bays keep the North fed. [ROOT.GetName] salts and stores both against the long winter, and the winter finds it ready.

focuses.name: Market Fairs
focuses.desc: At midsummer the crown holds a fair on the common, and traders arrive from three coasts with wagons, mules and quarrels to settle. By week's end the quarrels are settled and the wagons are empty.

focuses.name: A Prosperous [ROOT.GetAdjective] Crown
focuses.desc: Granaries full, roads open and a treasury a little heavier than last year: the North has few finer things to boast of. [ROOT.GetName] builds one more workshop with the proceeds, and nobody grumbles at the tax.

focuses.name: Boats and Nets
focuses.desc: The sea gives the northern coast its bread and takes its sons in return. [ROOT.GetName] gives its fishers new nets and tarred hulls, and a place by the harbour wall where the widows may sell the catch.

focuses.name: Harbour Works
focuses.desc: Breakwaters of stacked stone, quays of oak and a slip for building hulls: the harbour of [ROOT.GetName] grows into a port that other crowns can find on a chart.

focuses.name: Watch the Waters
focuses.desc: Island fishers have begun to tell a tale of black sails in the far north. [ROOT.GetName] sends a few men to the headland to watch the horizon and report what they see.

focuses.name: Shore Towers
focuses.desc: Square towers of grey stone rise along the cape road, each with a brazier on its roof and a gallery for a watch of six. They are as much a comfort as a defence.

focuses.name: Galleys of the Crown
focuses.desc: Long, narrow galleys are built for the winter coast, where sails fail and oars do not. Their crews drill in the bay until the oars rise and fall as one.

focuses.name: The Shore Watch
focuses.desc: From the cape to the river mouth every beacon answers the next. [ROOT.GetName] keeps its shore in sight by day and night, and expects to be told before anyone else.

focuses.name: Hill Holds
focuses.desc: With no coast to guard, the crown guards its hills. Stone holds are raised or mended on the high ground above the capital, each with a well, a granary and a gate that one man can shut.

focuses.name: Forest Trails
focuses.desc: Hunters and charcoal burners know every trail of the northern forests, and the crown pays them to teach the rest. A lantern at a trailhead means safe lodging for anyone who knows the sign.

focuses.name: Mines in the Hills
focuses.desc: Iron and tin lie in veins under the hills, and the crown sinks new shafts where the old ones failed. The ore goes down the valley by cart in spring and by sledge in winter.

focuses.name: The Upland Levy
focuses.desc: Each hill farm sends one son to the muster in autumn, as each has done since the oldest roll. [ROOT.GetName] drills them through the winter, and they walk home in spring somewhat taller.

focuses.name: An Island Crown
focuses.desc: The sea is this crown's only road, its only wall and sometimes its only neighbour. [ROOT.GetName] takes the isle's long solitude for its own and builds its habits around it.

focuses.name: Island Steersmen
focuses.desc: The steersmen of the isles know every shoal and tide-race between here and the mainland, and carry the knowledge in rhymes rather than charts. [ROOT.GetName] pays them to teach it to its young captains.

focuses.name: The Isle Keeps
focuses.desc: Where a harbour is the only gate, a pair of stout keeps makes it a good one. Both sides of the harbour mouth now carry a stone tower, and a chain can be drawn between them.

focuses.name: The Freeholders' Moot
focuses.desc: Every free farmer of [ROOT.GetName] has a voice at the moot, and the moot meets in the open air so that none may say he did not hear. Decisions are slow, but they are kept.

focuses.name: Old Rights Kept
focuses.desc: The moot copies the old rights onto a long roll and reads them aloud each Glernaen. Every freeholder hears what he is owed, and what the crown is owed in return.

focuses.name: The Free Towns' Council
focuses.desc: The towns of [ROOT.GetName] have won their charters one by one and now sit together in a council of burghers. They tax themselves, build their own walls and write their own law.

focuses.name: Elected Wardens
focuses.desc: The council elects wardens for the roads, the walls and the weights, and takes them from office when they fail. Honest dealing is not universal, but it is expected.

focuses.name: A Lord's Hand
focuses.desc: One hand holds the crown now, and its grip is firm. The lord of [ROOT.GetName] sets aside the old moot's quarrels and tells the realm what it will do.

focuses.name: The Lord's Men
focuses.desc: Stewards, bailiffs and sworn knights hold the lord's land, and the lord's coin holds them. They are loyal while it lasts, and they make the realm run to the lord's measure.

focuses.name: Under the Leren Banner
focuses.desc: The banner of Lerendor flies over the capital beside the crown's own, and its garrison eats at the crown's table. [ROOT.GetName] learns the Leren drill, the Leren law and the Leren manner of waiting.

focuses.name: Leren Garrisons
focuses.desc: Sonargur sends engineers and masons to strengthen the crown's walls, and promises that the stones it lays will stand for the crown's sake as well as its own.

focuses.name: Sonargur's Trust
focuses.desc: Years of faithful service have earned the crown a seat at Sonargur's table. Its lord is asked before the great decisions are made, and told afterward about the small ones.

focuses.name: The Compact Member
focuses.desc: A seat in the Leren Compact brings a tall chair, a short oath and a long list of duties. [ROOT.GetName] takes the seat with some pride and the duties with some doubt.

focuses.name: Compact Fleet Duty
focuses.desc: In summer the Compact's ships gather at Sonargur, and the member crowns send hulls and crews to take their turn at the strait. The duty is dull and the pay is small, but it teaches a crew to keep station in a gale.

focuses.name: Compact Levies
focuses.desc: The Compact calls for companies, and [ROOT.GetName] sends its share by the autumn road. They come home in spring with new drill and a few stories nobody believes.

focuses.name: Kin of the North
focuses.desc: The men of the North are one people in many halls, and they trade marriages and quarrels in about equal measure. [ROOT.GetName] strengthens the old ties with a feast and a sworn year of peace with its neighbours.

focuses.name: Northern Levies
focuses.desc: Northern boys can swing an axe before they can read, and the crown puts the knack to use. A yearly muster teaches them to do it in line, in step and under orders.

focuses.name: Across the Dark Straits
focuses.desc: South-west across the narrow water lie the holds of the Dark Lands, and their orc captains look north often. [ROOT.GetName] keeps a sharp watch on the straits and a sharper eye on whoever crosses them.

focuses.name: Traders of the Dark Shore
focuses.desc: The orcs buy northern furs, salt fish and iron, and pay in silver that no one inquires about. The traders of [ROOT.GetName] go carefully, keep to the harbours and come home with full purses.

focuses.name: Whispers from the Holds
focuses.desc: Traders return from the Dark Lands with news that is not quite rumour and not quite truth. [ROOT.GetName] listens to all of it and decides later what to believe.

focuses.name: Temples and Almshouses
focuses.desc: The Houses of the First Light have opened almshouses in the northern towns, where grey-robed almoners sent by [zin_loc_deliverer] feed the hungry and tend the sick for nothing. [ROOT.GetName] grants them land for a hospital and a kitchen and takes their help gladly.

focuses.name: A Watchful Crown
focuses.desc: The almoners have friends in places where friends should not be, and the crown has noticed. [ROOT.GetName] keeps a quiet eye on the Houses and a quieter one on their ledgers, and asks no one to say why.

focuses.name: The North at War
focuses.desc: The beacons are lit, the horns are blown and the muster rolls are taken down from their pegs. For the first time in living memory the North must decide what it owes, and to whom.

focuses.name: Beacons on the Capes
focuses.desc: A line of fires on every cape lets the coast speak to itself faster than a rider can. [ROOT.GetName] doubles its watches and sends nobody to bed without a lit brand beside him.

focuses.name: Stand Apart with Sonargur
focuses.desc: The old alliance with the south is over, and the North stands apart from it. [ROOT.GetName] stays beside Sonargur, believing a lone crown easier to break than a hall of crowns.

focuses.name: Keep Faith with Parim
focuses.desc: Oaths sworn at the Narrow Strait are not dropped because a greater crown drops them. [ROOT.GetName] sends word to Parim that it holds to the old alliance, and asks what its companies might do.

focuses.name: Against the Deathless
focuses.desc: The dead that come out of the sea are slow, patient and not easily killed. [ROOT.GetName] drills its companies to cut them down, to burn what is left and to keep out of reach of the rest.

effects.tooltip: Ordinary arms break Zol's dead; they do not end them.

focuses.name: Northern Companies
focuses.desc: A banner has been raised in the south to which the lords of the North may bring their companies without bowing to anyone. [ROOT.GetName] sends its own under its own colours, and keeps the right to bring them home.

focuses.name: The Shore Is Quiet
focuses.desc: The beacons are out, the companies are home and the harbours slowly fill with ordinary ships again. [ROOT.GetName] counts its dead, mends its roofs and lets the shore be quiet.
